14.0.0.en: Shinar: it lies in northern Iraq between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

14.0.3.en: Goiim (nations): it lies northeast of Babylon (northern Iraq and southern Iran). Chedorlaomer: it means servant of Lagamar, who was one of the gods of the Elamites.

14.0.4.en: The power of Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, emerged, and he defeated many kings and subjected their cities to himself, as far as the land of Palestine, and they paid him tribute for 12 years. But some of them rebelled against him and refused to pay the tribute, so he set out, allied with three kings who lived around him, namely the kings of Shinar, Ellasar and Goiim, on a punitive campaign to subdue these rebels.

14.1.0.en: Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim: four cities lying south and west of the Dead Sea.

14.1.1.en: Zoar (Bela): it lies east of the Dead Sea.

14.1.2.en: The kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim united, and the king of Zoar joined them, and they rebelled against Chedorlaomer, refusing to pay him tribute. So he rose against them to fight them and subdue them to himself again, and they united together to fight him.

14.2.0.en: The Valley of Siddim: a plain beside the Dead Sea, which is called the Salt Sea or Lot's lake. It is called the Valley of Siddim because pits and fissures abound in the ground there.

14.2.1.en: The five kings mentioned in (v. 2), that is, the king of Sodom and those with him, went out to fight Chedorlaomer and those with him, and took their stand in a plain called the Valley of Siddim.

14.3.0.en: It was explained before in (v. 1). After Chedorlaomer had enslaved the kings of Sodom and those around it for 12 years, they rebelled against him in the thirteenth year.

14.4.0.en: Chedorlaomer prepared with an army united with the three kings who lived around him, and they came to fight the king of Sodom and those with him in the fourteenth year. When they drew near to Sodom, they fought some countries on their way to Sodom, countries lying east of the Dead Sea, namely the Rephaim, the Zuzim and the Emim, in order to subdue them to himself and to frighten the king of Sodom and those with him, so as to make sure they would not support the king of Sodom and that no king in the region would try to stand against him.

14.5.0.en: Then Chedorlaomer turned south toward the Horites who lived in Mount Seir, extending from the Gulf of Aqaba to the Dead Sea, and defeated them in the plain of Paran, northwest of the Gulf of Aqaba.

14.6.0.en: Then Chedorlaomer returned, heading north, and defeated the Amalekites and the Amorites west of the Dead Sea at En-mishpat, which is Kadesh, and then at the strongholds of Hazazon-tamar, very near the western side of the Dead Sea.

14.7.0.en: Battle was joined between Chedorlaomer and the three kings with him, against the king of Sodom and the four kings with him.

14.8.0.en: Chedorlaomer defeated the five kings, that is, the king of Sodom and those with him, in the Valley of Siddim, which is full of fissures and pits, and in which there were also slime pits, which is mineral bitumen. So the armies of the king of Sodom and those with him fled, and many of them fell and perished in the slime pits, and the rest of the armies fled to the surrounding mountains.

14.9.0.en: When the armies of the king of Sodom and the armies united with him fled, the armies of Chedorlaomer entered and seized their country, took its inhabitants captive and plundered their spoils; and among the captives was Lot, who lived in their country.

14.9.1.en: Lot loved the fertile land and was content to live in Sodom, which was full of evil and enslaved to Chedorlaomer, so his heart was tormented by the evils he saw. And since he did not repent and move away from it, God allowed him a severe affliction, namely his being seized as a captive when his country was defeated before Chedorlaomer, and he gained nothing from the wealth and comfort but entered into the affliction of captivity. I wish, my brother, that you would not drift with the current of the world which pursues money, for it is bound up with evil and exposed to many afflictions that God allows for you, perhaps that you may repent; and if afflictions meet you, return quickly to the love of God and put away the love of money.

14.10.0.en: Some of the people of Sodom escaped, and one of them came to Abram to tell him that his nephew Lot had been taken captive with many of the prisoners, because of Chedorlaomer's victory over the five kings. Abram moved quickly and gathered from his servants 318 men trained for war, young men who were born in his house because their fathers were servants of his. This teaches us the strength of Abram, who had many servants who herded and guarded the livestock he owned, and he chose 318 of them for the war.

14.10.1.en: Abram was living beside the Amorites, among whose chiefs were the three brothers Mamre, Eshcol and Aner, and there was a peace treaty between Abram and them. When they learned what had happened to Abram's nephew, they showed their readiness to help him because of the treaty between them and him, and a considerable number of them went out with Abram, as appears from (v. 24). Some of the Fathers say that just as the 318 men of Abram's servants rescued Lot and all the captives, so the 318 bishops gathered at Nicaea rescued the Church from the heresy of Arius.

14.10.2.en: Abram himself went out with the fighters, although his age at that time was over eighty, but because of his detachment in the wilderness God filled his heart with zeal and love for the weak and needy, so he went out by God's power to rescue his nephew Lot and those with him.

14.11.0.en: Abram headed north to overtake the armies of Chedorlaomer, and reached them at Dan, which lies in the north of Palestine. He made ready and attacked them by night, dividing himself into two companies to surround them in his attack. He struck them a severe blow while they were asleep and defeated them, so they fled from him, and he pursued them to the city of Hobah, which lies near Damascus (the present capital of Syria).

14.12.0.en: Abram was able to rescue Lot and the captives with him and to recover the spoils that Chedorlaomer had taken, and he returned with them to his place.

14.12.1.en: In proportion as you detach yourself from material things and depend on God, you receive strength and your heart opens in love toward others, so you become influential on all around you and draw them by your life to Christ.

14.13.s.en: (3) Melchizedek and the king of Sodom

14.13.0.en: The Valley of Shaveh: a deep plain lying north of Jerusalem at a distance of a quarter of a mile, and it is called the King's Valley because kings used to gather in it.

14.13.1.en: The news of Abram's victory over Chedorlaomer and those with him, and his bringing back of the captives and the spoils, reached them, and the kings who had been defeated rejoiced greatly. Their chief, the king of Sodom, went out to meet Abram returning from the region of Damascus, and met him north of Jerusalem in a plain called the Valley of Shaveh.

14.14.0.en: Melchizedek also went out to meet Abram. He was king of Salem or Shalem, that is, Jerusalem, and was a priest at the same time. He offered a strange offering, not animal sacrifices as people were accustomed and as God had taught Adam; this offering was bread and wine, which is of course the sacrifice of the New Testament, that is, the Body and Blood of Christ. He is therefore a clear type of Christ, for which the Jews are unable to offer an explanation.

14.15.0.en: Melchizedek blessed Abram, who was returning after his victory, with a blessing from God Most High and not by the gods of the Gentiles, at a time when no one worshipped God except Abram, and all around him in the world were pagans. This confirms that he is a clear type of Christ, to whom Abram, the father of the Jewish people, submitted, from whom came the Aaronic priesthood, that is, the priesthood of the Jews. The meaning of this is that Melchizedek, that is, Christ, is the one who blesses the Jewish priesthood, that is, that the priesthood of Christ is higher than the Jewish priesthood, as the Epistle to the Hebrews makes clear (Heb 7).

14.16.0.en: Melchizedek made clear that the victor was God, by the hand of Abram; the cause of the power was not Abram but God working in him. So Abram rejoiced in this blessing and submitted to Melchizedek and gave him a tenth of the spoils he had brought after his victory over Chedorlaomer.

14.16.1.en: Melchizedek was a type of Christ, as appears in the following:

14.16.2.en: 1- Melchizedek was king of Salem, that is, the city of peace, and Christ is the King of peace, indeed the King of kings.

14.16.3.en: 2- Melchizedek was priest and king at the same time, and Christ is the Great High Priest who offered the sacrifice of Himself on the cross, and He is Priest and King at the same time like Melchizedek.

14.16.4.en: 3- The Holy Bible mentions no father or mother or genealogy for Melchizedek, like Christ, who has no bodily father and also no mother with regard to His divinity, and who was born in the fullness of time but has existed from eternity.

14.16.5.en: 4- Melchizedek offered a sacrifice of bread and wine, like the sacrifice of Christ in the New Testament, which is bread and wine and not animal sacrifices.

14.16.6.en: 5- Melchizedek blessed Abram, the father of the people of God, and Christ blesses His people, the Christians who believe in Him.

14.17.0.en: If Abram had defeated Chedorlaomer and those with him, he had the right to take the spoils and even the captives, but because the king of Sodom knew Abram's love and breadth of heart, he asked him to give him the captives and to be content with the spoils.

14.18.1.en: Abram raised his heart in prayer to God, the source of his strength and blessing, and then said to the king of Sodom what he did not expect, for he said to him: take the captives and also all the spoils, and I will take nothing of it, even something small, so that all of Abram's wealth may be from God, and neither the king of Sodom nor any person may think that he was the cause of his riches.

14.18.2.en: It is to be noted here that this is the first time a person declares an oath, "I have raised my hand to the Lord, God Most High, the Possessor of heaven and earth," and the first time a priest is mentioned, and likewise the first mention of a war.

14.19.0.en: Abram completed his speech to the king of Sodom, saying that he would take nothing of the spoils except what the men of war had eaten on the way from the spoils, so that they would not faint. And although Abram had given up all his rights, his partners in the war did not lose their rights, namely the chiefs of the Amorites, that is, Mamre and his brothers and the fighters with them. Here appear Abram's justice and his respect for the rights of others.

14.19.1.en: Trust in God's blessing for you, for in proportion as you give up, God blesses you and enriches you, so that you need no person, but you are a blessing to those around you and help every needy one.

14.19.2.en: See the map at the end of the book.

14.19.3.en: God's covenant with Abram and the divided sacrifices

15.0.0.en: Shield: a wooden piece covered with leather and having a handle through which the soldier puts his hand; the shield is used to ward off the arrows cast at him, protecting his face and body with it.

15.0.1.en: God appeared to Abram for the fifth time while he was inside his tent by night. It is clear from this that God appeared to him many times, so that he was called a friend of God, because he detached himself from the world, lived in the wilderness and devoted himself to knowing God, so God appeared to him often and they became friends. God's speech with him includes three matters:

15.0.2.en: 1- Do not be afraid: of Chedorlaomer and all who are with him, should they try to fight you, for I am with you. And do not be afraid either of the tribes around you or of anything that comes upon your life.

15.0.3.en: 2- I am your shield: God offers Himself as protection for Abraham, like the shield with which a soldier protects himself. And as the shield moves to protect the soldier, whether his head or his body, how much more God, who surrounds Abram and protects him with complete protection.

15.0.4.en: 3- Your reward shall be exceedingly great: if you, Abram, have given up the spoils that you took from Chedorlaomer, then in proportion to your self-restraint I give you a blessing that no mind can imagine, namely that your seed will be like the stars of heaven and you will be a blessing to the whole world through Christ, who comes from your seed.

15.0.5.en: Always remember your strong and loving God, who protects you and keeps you in all your steps, so do not be troubled by the changes of the world or the threats of the wicked or the unknown future. Always remember, and repeat every day, God's word to Abram, "I am your shield."

15.1.0.en: Abram rejoiced at God's appearing to him, and with the boldness of love and friendship he asked Him about the details of the great reward, since he was not content with possessions but reminded Him of His promise to give him offspring, although up to now he had no son, but if he died his closest servant, the chief of his servants, Eliezer of Damascus, who was born in his house because his father and mother were his servants, would inherit him.

15.2.0.en: God declared to Abram that He would give him offspring from his wife Sarah, and that none of his servants would inherit him.

15.3.0.en: To confirm God's promise, He brought Abram out of the tent by night and said to him, look toward the stars of heaven and try to count them. They are of course very many and cannot be numbered; so shall your seed be, as numerous as the stars, and it cannot be counted.

15.4.0.en: Here appears Abraham's great faith in God. Although the word surpasses reason, since he is an old man and God promises him offspring that cannot be counted, he believed, and this became a proof of his righteousness and goodness.

15.5.0.en: God repeated His promise to him to give him the land of Canaan as an inheritance for him and his seed, as He had told him when He brought him out of his city Ur of the Chaldees.

15.6.0.en: Abram's question was not doubt but a request for a sign, for he did not say how but whereby, just as the Lady the Virgin asked the angel Gabriel about her giving birth to Christ while she wished to remain a virgin, and he informed her that the birth is from the Holy Spirit and not from a man.

15.6.1.en: Have boldness before God and ask Him for what you wish, so that He may confirm your faith and support you, for He is your Father who loves you. And if any doubt about God's word fights against you, repeat any psalm or prayer so that you may stand firm in your faith.

15.7.0.en: People in that time were accustomed to make their covenants by slaughtering an animal, cutting it in two and placing the halves on the two sides, with the covenanting parties passing between them as a proof of confirming the covenant. This is a type of the blood of Christ, which confirms the covenant between us and God, and which we partake of in the New Testament as true Body and Blood. So God asked Abram to make a covenant with Him in the same manner that people made in his time, and asked him to bring a heifer three years old, a female goat also three years old, and likewise a ram of the same age, and to cut the three, each into two halves, and place each half opposite the other, leaving a space between them for him and God to pass between. God also asked him to slaughter a turtledove and a pigeon without dividing them, and perhaps he placed them one opposite the other on the two sides.

15.7.1.en: Their being three years old is a symbol of the Holy Trinity. The animals signify souls that incline to animal desires, and the birds signify souls that incline to heavenly things; and the dividing of the animals signifies the divisions and factions that occur among those who incline to desires and the world, whereas among the spiritual no divisions occur.

15.8.0.en: Abram slaughtered the sacrifices, divided them and placed them from the morning, waiting for God to appear in the form He saw fit so that He might pass with him between the divided sacrifices. The birds of prey drew near trying to eat these sacrifices, so Abram sat beside them, watchful, and drove them away.

15.8.1.en: The birds of prey signify the evil thoughts that attack a person and that he cannot prevent, but he can drive them away by prayer and by asking God's help.

15.9.0.en: Abram waited all day for God to appear until the sun went down. Then he fell into a deep sleep and felt in his sleep a great fear and darkness, that is, obscurity, because he did not know what God would say to him and how He would appear and make the covenant with him. This shows the fear of God that was in his heart in spite of his enjoying friendship and boldness with Him.

15.10.0.en: God spoke with Abram and informed him of the future of his seed: that they would go to a foreign country and the people of that country would enslave them for 400 years. God did not mention the name of the country, which is Egypt, so that they would not be afraid to go there.

15.11.0.en: God promises to judge this nation, that is, Egypt, which enslaves the seed of Abraham, and this is what happened in the ten plagues and the drowning of Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea. He also promised him that his seed would take great possessions, which are the jewelry and clothing that they borrowed from the Egyptians, who gave them in abundance and let them go out quickly with them so that God's wrath upon them might stop.

15.12.0.en: God informed Abraham that he would die before these afflictions came upon his seed, and that he would die in a good old age, that is, in peace, after a blessed life and a pure life with God.

15.13.0.en: God also promised that the seed of Abraham would return to the land of Canaan in the fourth generation, that is, after four centuries, where they would destroy the inhabitants of the land of Canaan and take possession of their lands. The reason for delaying the possession of the land of Canaan by Abram's seed for 400 years was to give the Amorites an opportunity to repent; and if they did not repent, their iniquity would be complete and they would exhaust all their opportunities for repentance, so God would destroy them by the hand of Joshua and those after him.

15.14.0.en: After God finished speaking with Abram about the future of his seed, the sun had completely set and darkness covered the earth. Then there appeared a pillar of fire surrounded by smoke, which passed between the divided sacrifices, and this was a divine appearance, because our God is a consuming fire who rejects all evil, and He is strong and able to fulfil His covenant and crush everyone who resists Abram. God alone passed between the divided sacrifices and did not take Abram with Him, because man is liable to error and to going back on the covenant, so God alone made the covenant to confirm its effect and fulfilment.

15.15.0.en: This is the rest of God's word to Abram, for He promised him that his seed would possess the lands from the river Euphrates to the river of Egypt, which is a seasonal river that fills with rainwater and floods and lies in Sinai.

15.16.0.en: God mentioned the peoples who live in the land that the seed of Abraham would possess, and they are:

15.16.1.en: 1- The Kenites: they lived in the land of Midian, east of Sinai.

15.16.2.en: 2- The Kenizzites: the meaning is hunters, and they are among the Canaanite tribes.

15.16.3.en: 3- The Kadmonites: their meaning is the ancients.

15.17.0.en: 4- The Hittites: the sons of Heth the son of Canaan, who lived in the south of the land of Canaan.

15.17.1.en: 5- The Perizzites: that is, the villagers, who lived in scattered places in the land of Canaan.

15.17.2.en: 6- The Rephaim: that is, the giants, who lived first east of the Jordan and then were driven out and lived in western Palestine.

15.18.0.en: 7- The Amorites: that is, the mountain dwellers because they lived in the mountains.

15.18.1.en: 8- The Canaanites: named after Canaan the son of Ham, and they lived in the cities throughout the land of Canaan.

15.18.2.en: 9- The Girgashites: they lived east of the Sea of Galilee in the north of Palestine.

15.18.3.en: 10- The Jebusites: they lived in Jerusalem and around it.

15.18.4.en: God's blessing is great for His children, but if the matter requires, He allows them afflictions for a limited time for the sake of their salvation. So accept affliction with thanksgiving so that it brings you nearer to God, and trust that because of your submission to Him He will bless you and compensate you with great blessings.
